name: HiddenDifference
source:
They do n't know me. They never did. Nor did they ever try to. Who are they to judge me? They have no idea what kind of personal Hell I've had to drudge through because of my appearance. It is n't fair. 
 
 My mother and father, bless them so, gave birth to me. They knew what was to come, but they truly had no idea. They kept me indoors, behind closed curtains and locked doors for fear of harassment, and yet, it still happened. 
 
 Word always traveled fast, and no one knew how. Angry letters, threats, and not a single well-wisher. All because I was this, freak. 
 
 I still needed an education, so they taught me. The days were short and allowed me to do what I wanted after. But at what cost? I could n't go outside to play with the other children. I knew all too well that they'd point and laugh, or scream and run to the comforting arms of their parents. 
 
 The endless nights of crying myself to sleep became like clockwork. Never could I drift away into the blackened bliss of sleep without shedding a single tear. Why is this world full of hate? I just want to be normal. 
 
 What is normal? To have no imperfections? To have a good job, nice home and family to complete the bundle? Why ca n't I have those things? Why am I the only one who has to be kept away? That's right, because I'm different. But no more. 
 
 No more will I hang my head in shame, shrouded underneath my hoodie. Never again shall I tuck my tail so no one can see. I'm done. If I am to live in this world, I am to do so with the intent to live a peaceful and fruitful life. No one can tell me otherwise. This is my life, and I'm going to live it like I want to. Today is the day I step outside of my comfort zone without the covers and embrace the world. Today, I start my new life.
retelling:
From the perspective of **Mother**, the tale unfolds as a poignant narrative of resilience and love. Behind closed curtains and locked doors, my heart ached for the life my child deserved. The world outside was cruel and unforgiving, yet I could not shield them entirely from its harsh realities.

The home, our sanctuary, was their prison - a place of safety, but also of confinement. My husband and I tried to create an oasis of love, filling it with books, music, and laughter, yet the darkness that seeped in from the outside world threatened to consume us all.

I watched as my child struggled, grappling with their emotions, their dreams, and their hopes. The anger and sadness they harbored were palpable, a weight on their fragile shoulders. Yet, amidst this turmoil, I saw glimmers of resolve, flashes of hope.

Their education, home-bound, was an attempt to keep them safe, to provide them with the knowledge they needed to navigate the world. But it was also a constant reminder of the life we denied them. They yearned for friends, for laughter echoing through our hallways, for the freedom to explore beyond our walls.

The letters that arrived were vile and hateful, yet I read every word, feeling each blow as if it were meant for me. But my child, strong and courageous, bore the brunt of these attacks with unyielding resilience. Their spirit was indomitable, a beacon of hope in our darkest hours.

As I watch them now, standing tall, their head held high, I cannot help but feel a swell of pride. They have endured more than most could bear, yet they refuse to be defined by their circumstances. Their determination to live freely, openly confronting the prejudice they faced, is a testament to their strength and spirit.

In my heart, I know that this journey will not be easy. The world outside remains hostile and unforgiving. But as a mother, I have faith in my child's ability to overcome adversity and find joy. Their story is one of courage, resilience, and love - a story I am honored to witness unfold.
